title: Scaling New Approaches to Learn-Work Transitions for People with Special Support Needs
content: The number of young people with support needs (YSSN) is increasing across European countries, including the Netherlands and Belgium, while the disability employment gap persists despite policy efforts. Transitions from school and care to work and adult life remain challenging, shaped by complex regulations, changing responsibilities and fragmented services. This study explores what YSSN themselves identify as important for meaningful participation, using an arts-based research approach with graphical elicitation, informed by Schalock’s Quality of Life model (2000). The approach creates space for young people to express experiences, aspirations and needs that may remain less visible through conventional methods. Their accounts particularly highlight a desire to be meaningful to others and to contribute to their communities and working environments, suggesting that work is valued not only as employment but as a context for belonging, contribution, and recognition. These findings inform two innovative care-work-learn approaches that are being scaled through action research in regional transition arenas involving (young) people, families, professionals and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs). The arenas support professionals to explore integrated approaches that develop young people’s strengths and participation in regular work environments. The project aims to inform teachers, education and training programmes on how to prepare young people with disabilities for a meaningful life, grounded in their own voices, aspirations and contributions.
